components.name: Use My Location Action
components.description: Labeled location action paired with a semantic location mark.
components.css: .ds-location-action { min-height:42px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:0 10px; color:var(--text-primary); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--hairline-strong); border-radius:3px; font:400 .84rem var(--font-ui); } .ds-location-action svg { width:17px; height:17px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:1.6; } .ds-location-action:hover { background:var(--canvas-secondary); } .ds-location-action:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Location Search
components.description: Plain-language place search with region and country in each result.
components.html: <form class="ds-location-search" role="search"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><circle cx="8.5" cy="8.5" r="5.5"/><path d="m13 13 4 4"/></svg><input aria-label="Search location" placeholder="Search city or place"></form>
components.css: .ds-location-search { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; height:42px; padding:0 11px; color:var(--text-muted); background:var(--panel-raised); border:1px solid var(--hairline-strong); border-radius:3px; } .ds-location-search svg { width:16px; height:16px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:1.6; } .ds-location-search input { min-width:0; flex:1; height:100%; color:var(--text-primary); background:transparent; border:0; font:400 0.88rem var(--font-ui); } .ds-location-search:focus-within { outline:3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Primary Navigation
components.description: Five labeled destinations remain visible on desktop and mobile.
components.html: CurrentForecastMapHistoryAlerts
components.css: .ds-primary-nav { display:flex; gap:4px; font:550 0.9rem var(--font-ui); } .ds-primary-nav a { min-height:42px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; padding:8px 13px; color:var(--text-secondary); text-decoration:none; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:3px; } .ds-primary-nav a:hover, .ds-primary-nav a[aria-current=page] { color:var(--accent); background:var(--canvas-secondary); border-color:var(--hairline); } .ds-primary-nav a:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Hourly Timeline Entry
components.description: Compact forecast time, semantic condition asset, temperature, and rain chance.
components.css: .ds-hour { min-height:138px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:8px; padding:11px 6px 9px; border-left:1px solid var(--hairline); color:var(--text-secondary); text-align:center; } .ds-hour strong { color:var(--text-primary); font:550 1.04rem var(--font-data); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-hour small { color:var(--accent); font:400 .7rem var(--font-data); }

narrative.overview:
WeatherWatch is a practical observation of the weather where someone is now. The interface reads like a calm, well-kept field log: the place and update state establish context, current conditions are unmistakable, and time-based forecasts follow in a continuous sequence. It is designed for people checking the weather while planning an ordinary day, not for interpreting a technical dashboard.

A single atmospheric scene gives the current reading physical depth without competing with its meaning. Real condition and measurement SVGs identify weather and data; typography, spacing, and rules do most of the organizing. Secondary routes retain the same navigation and state vocabulary for forecasts, map, history, and alerts.
keyCharacteristics: Mineral-light ground, charcoal text, and one measured weather-blue interaction color.
Tabular figures are reserved for temperatures, measurements, and times.
Open information groups and fine dividers replace repeated metric cards.
A restrained weather environment sits behind the current reading only.
Location, forecast, risk, provider, and unavailable states are named in plain language.

rules.name: The Signal Economy Rule
rules.body: Weather blue means interaction; green, ochre, rust, and red retain severity meaning. Do not use status colors as decoration.

rules.name: The Explicit State Rule
rules.body: Loading, unavailable, permission-blocked, provider-dependent, and application-generated information is identified in words and never styled as a confirmed observation.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Use the data face for measured values and timestamps; use the interface face for meaning, labels, and navigation.

rules.name: The One Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: Keep motion and dimensional depth inside the current weather environment; the information itself remains still.

rules.name: The Selective Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass is reserved for the current reading, location search/results, and controls over map imagery. Forecast rows, metric rows, labels, and notices remain flat.

dos: Show the selected place and local update context before the temperature.
Keep feels-like and today's high/low beside current conditions.
Label each forecast value and keep rain probability beside its time period.
Use the provided weather SVGs for conditions and matching measurements.
Preserve real provider, loading, permission, risk, and unavailable states.
Respect reduced motion and keep the weather information stationary.
donts: Hide hourly conditions behind a tab on the Current page.
Make every value an icon-and-number card.
Use weather icon artwork as the only condition label.
Imply that a disconnected official warning source has confirmed “no alerts.”
Add motion to the page, forecast rows, or measurements.
